params.body:
Laying an operator-signed admission down at Portal (`POST ingest/workbench/admitted/{slug}`, the door the YubiKey's word goes through) answered 500 the first time it was ever used, today, for Vera's machine. The reason was nowhere near the door: `OperatorKeys::published()` caches the operator's keys as raw 32 bytes, the cache store in production is the database, and its `value` column is text, so MySQL refused the whole write with `Incorrect string value: '\xBF\xB1\x84...'`.

- What is cached is now the key as the document writes it, base64url; the caller still gets the raw bytes.
- The test reads the cached shape rather than the store's behaviour, because the suite runs on the array store and would never have seen this.

The door matters beyond the workbench: Vera's own machine holds the read token, and a review ticket is issued only while an admission stands, so an admission that cannot be kept means that machine cannot act at all.
params.title: Toelating op het token: de sleutels als tekst in de cache
